faq.q: Can I consider a cash offer while my house is listed?
faq.a: You can evaluate an offer, but your listing agreement and any existing sale contract need to be reviewed before you commit. Tell your listing broker about the proposal and clarify fees and any required arrangements.

faq.q: Does finding my own buyer mean I owe no broker fee?
faq.a: Do not assume that. The signed listing agreement, amendments and any release determine the obligations to review. A direct buyer's pricing does not cancel a separate agreement with your broker.

faq.q: Does removing the online listing cancel the agreement?
faq.a: Treat marketing status and the signed agreement as separate questions. Obtain the documents establishing any agreed termination or release and review whether fees or other terms remain.

faq.q: Should I wait for the listing to expire before accepting an offer?
faq.a: There is no universal answer. Review the term, any post-listing obligations, the proposed buyer and your timing needs with the broker or your attorney before deciding. Expiration alone should not be treated as proof that every obligation has ended.
